cheat_sheet.title: Noun Complete Revision Cheat Sheet
cheat_sheet.subtitle: All 23 Core Rules, Golden Formulas, Complete Word Lists & Exam Traps

rules.title: Always Plural Nouns (Take Plural Verb)
rules.description: These nouns are always used in the plural form only and cannot be made singular by removing 's'/'es'. They always take a plural verb.

ssc_traps.correct: Where are my scissors?
All his belongings were lost.
I bought a pair of spectacles.

rules.key_note: To indicate singular count, use 'a pair of...'. When 'a pair of' is used as the subject, the verb becomes singular ('A pair of trousers was bought').

rules.title: Plural in Form, but Singular in Meaning (Take Singular Verb)
rules.description: These nouns end in 's' and look plural, but their meaning is singular and they always take a singular verb.

ssc_traps.correct: Mathematics is a difficult subject.
No news is good news.
He was issued a summons (Singular = summons; Plural = summonses).

rules.special_exception: When subjects like Mathematics, Politics, Statistics are preceded by a possessive adjective (my, his, our) or 'the' to mean calculations, political views, or data, they take a PLURAL verb: 'His mathematics are very weak', 'The statistics of the survey reveal...'

rules.title: Singular in Form, but Always Plural in Meaning (Take Plural Verb)
rules.description: These nouns look singular because they lack an 's' ending, but they are plural in sense and always take a plural verb. Never add '-s' or '-es' to them.

ssc_traps.incorrect: Cattles are grazing in the field.
ssc_traps.correct: Cattle are grazing in the field (Never say 'cattles').
Police have caught the thief.
Our infantry have marched forward.

rules.special_exception: 'People' means human beings. 'Peoples' is used ONLY when referring to nations/ethnic groups of the world.

rules.title: Uncountable Nouns (Always Singular Verb, No a/an, No -s/-es)
rules.formula: Uncountable Noun + Singular Verb [Never take a/an, never take -s/-es]
rules.description: These nouns are strictly uncountable. They cannot be pluralized by adding 's' and never take indefinite articles (a/an) directly.

ssc_traps.incorrect: The sceneries of Kashmir are beautiful.
ssc_traps.correct: The scenery of Kashmir is beautiful.
He gave me a piece of advice.

ssc_traps.incorrect: I have many works to do.
ssc_traps.correct: I have much work to do (or: many pieces of work).
Furniture was sold.

rules.countability_modifiers: To express count, use: 'a piece of advice', 'two pieces of information', 'an article of luggage', 'a loaf of bread'.

rules.title: Usage of 'Hair' (Uncountable vs Countable)
rules.formula: All hair on head = Uncountable (Singular) | Individual strands = Countable (Plural)
rules.description: Hair is normally considered an uncountable collective noun taking a singular verb. However, when counting specific individual strands, it can be pluralized.

ssc_traps.correct: His hair is black.

ssc_traps.incorrect: She found two hair in the soup.
ssc_traps.correct: She found two hairs in the soup (Countable strands).

rules.title: Nouns with Identical Singular & Plural Forms
rules.formula: Same Spelling for 1 or Many (Verb depends on context)
rules.description: These nouns do not change form in the plural. Their verb is determined by whether the context refers to one or many.

ssc_traps.incorrect: A sheep is grazing / Sheeps are grazing.
ssc_traps.correct: A sheep is grazing / Sheep are grazing (Never 'sheeps').
Many deer were seen (Never 'deers').
A new series is launched / Two new series are launched.

rules.special_exception: 'Fishes' is only used when referring to different species or varieties of fish, not total quantity.

rules.title: [The + Common Noun] Expressing an Abstract Quality
rules.description: When 'the' is prefixed to a common noun representing a person or relation, it denotes the inner emotion, instinct, or characteristic (functioning as an abstract noun).

examples.sentence: The judge in him prevailed over the father.
examples.explanation: 'The judge' = sense of justice; 'the father' = fatherly affection.

examples.sentence: The mother in her arose when she saw the crying orphan.

rules.title: Plural of Nouns Ending in '-ful'
rules.description: Nouns ending in 'ful' are pluralized by adding 's' at the very end of 'ful', NOT to the base noun.

ssc_traps.incorrect: He drank three cupsful of coffee.
ssc_traps.correct: He drank three cupfuls of coffee.
Take two spoonfuls of syrup.

rules.title: Precise Usage of 'Half'
rules.formula: Half an hour / A half-hour | Two and a half hours / Two hours and a half
rules.description: Specific structural conventions govern how 'half' pairs with time and units:
rules: • 'Half an hour' OR 'A half-hour' (NOT 'A half an hour')
• 'Two and a half hours' OR 'Two hours and a half'

ssc_traps.incorrect: I waited for a half an hour.
ssc_traps.correct: I waited for half an hour (or a half-hour).

rules.title: Hyphenated Compound Nouns Used as Adjectives
rules.description: When a compound noun with a numeral functions as an adjective before another noun, the hyphenated noun must ALWAYS be singular.
rules.key_note: If not modifying another noun, the noun is plural: 'He gave me ten rupees'.

rules.title: Definite vs Indefinite Counting Nouns (Dozen, Hundred, Thousand...)
rules.formula: Definite Number + Dozen/Hundred/Million + Noun (Singular) | Dozens/Hundreds + of + Noun (Plural)
rules.description: Words like dozen, score, hundred, thousand, million, billion remain SINGULAR when preceded by an exact number. They take '-s' and 'of' only when indefinite.

ssc_traps.correct: I bought two dozen bananas.
Three thousand people attended.

ssc_traps.correct_indefinite: Dozens of bananas were spoiled / Thousands of people attended.

rules.title: 'The + Adjective' Representing a Whole Class
rules.formula: 'The' + Adjective = Plural Common Noun + Plural Verb
rules.description: When 'the' is placed before adjectives like poor, rich, blind, deaf, educated, sick, it denotes all people in that category. It acts as a plural noun and takes a plural verb. Never add '-s' to the adjective.

ssc_traps.correct: The poor are honest (Never say 'the poors').
The rich exploit the poor.

rules.title: 'The + Plural Surname' Denoting the Whole Family
rules.description: Preceding a pluralized family name with 'The' refers to the entire family as a group, requiring a plural verb.

examples.sentence: The Sharmas have gone on vacation.
examples.explanation: Refers to the entire Sharma family.
Refers to all members of the Gupta family.

rules.title: Frequent Superfluous / Slang Noun Errors in SSC
rules.description: Expressions common in colloquial Indian English that are strictly incorrect in Standard English:

pairs.incorrect: He is my cousin brother / cousin sister.
pairs.correct: He is my cousin / She is my cousin.

rules.title: Repeated Nouns Connected by a Preposition
rules.formula: Singular Noun + Preposition + Same Singular Noun + Singular Verb
rules.description: When the same noun is repeated on either side of a preposition, both nouns MUST be in singular form, and the verb MUST be singular.

ssc_traps.correct: Page after page was read.
Door to door was visited.

ssc_traps.incorrect: Rows upon rows of marble looks beautiful.
ssc_traps.correct: Row upon row of marble looks beautiful.

rules.title: Common Gender Nouns & Default Pronoun
rules.formula: Common Gender Noun (Teacher, Doctor, Student, Clerk, Leader) -> Default Pronoun 'He/His'
rules.description: When the gender of a common noun is unknown or unspecified, traditional grammatical convention uses the masculine third-person pronoun (he/his/him), NOT 'it' or 'they'.

examples.sentence: Every student must submit his assignment on time.

rules.title: Noun Gender & Personified Gender Laws
rules.description: Rules for masculine, feminine, and personified objects:

sections.Adding '-ess' with vowel drops: Actor → Actress, Hunter → Huntress, Waiter → Waitress, Master → Mistress

examples.sentence: The Sun shed his beams upon rich and poor alike.
The Moon hid her face behind a cloud.

rules.title: High-Frequency SSC Collective Nouns
groups: A pack of wolves / hounds / cards
A litter of puppies / kittens / pigs
A fleet of ships / motor cars
A swarm of bees / flies / ants

rules.title: Singular to Plural Formation Traps & Compound Plurals
rules: 1. Nouns ending in 'o' preceded by vowel add 's' (Radio → Radios, Video → Videos, Bamboo → Bamboos).
2. Compound Nouns: Pluralize the HEAD / ROOT WORD, not the tail word:

rules.title: Foreign Origin Noun Plurals (Greek / Latin Traps)

ssc_traps.correct: All the data was/were lost (Never say 'datas').

ssc_traps.incorrect: What is the criteria for selection?
ssc_traps.correct: What is the criterion for selection? (Singular = criterion).
This is a natural phenomenon (Singular = phenomenon).

rules.title: Compound Nouns Always Used in Plural Form
rules.example: He has a keen interest in current affairs (NOT current affair).

rules.title: Complete Noun Meaning Shifts when Pluralized (-s)
Comprehensive Apostrophe ('s) Laws
sub_rules: i) Used for Living Beings: 'Boy's book', 'Cow's milk'. For Non-Living things, NEVER use 's — use 'of': 'The leg of the table' (NOT 'table's leg'), 'The cover of the book' (NOT 'book's cover').

ii) Exceptions where Non-Living CAN take 's: Personified objects ('Nature's laws', 'Fortune's favorites'), Time/Space/Weight ('A day's leave', 'A mile's distance', 'A pound's weight'), Dignified celestial bodies ('The earth's surface', 'The sun's rays'), and established Idioms ('At one's wit's end', 'At an arm's length', 'At a stone's throw').
iii) Nouns ending in 's' or hissing sound: Only add the apostrophe (') without 's': 'Keats' poems', 'Dickens' novels', 'For conscience' sake', 'For peace' sake', 'Boys' school'.

iv) Joint Possession vs Separate Possession: If two nouns possess something jointly, add 's to the second noun only ('Ram and Shyam's father'). If they possess different items, add 's to both ('Ram's and Shyam's fathers').
v) Compound Nouns: Apostrophe is added to the LAST word only: 'Father-in-law's house', 'Commander-in-chief's order' (NOT 'Father's-in-law').

vi) Pronouns that NEVER take an Apostrophe: Possessive pronouns (hers, ours, yours, theirs, its, whose) NEVER take an apostrophe. 'Yours faithfully' (NOT 'Your's faithfully'). 'Its color' (possessive) vs 'It's' (= It is).
vii) 'Else' following Indefinite Pronouns: When 'else' follows somebody, anybody, nobody, someone, anyone, put the apostrophe on 'else': 'Somebody else's book' (NOT 'Somebody's else').

questions.question: (a) Rohit came / (b)with three / (c) cupsful of tea / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'cupsful' with 'cupfuls'. Nouns ending with 'ful' are made plural by putting 's' after 'ful'.

questions.question: (a) Rahul has given her / (b) thirty five millions dollars to / (c)buy a new house / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'millions' with 'million'. The noun 'million' is used as singular when used after a numeral.

questions.question: (a) I gifted him / (b) many pair / (c)of shoes / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'pair' with 'pairs'. Pair, dozen, thousand etc. are written in plural form when these words are used with Indefinite countable nouns like dozens of men, thousands of people, many pairs of socks, etc.

questions.question: (a) Deaf are / (b) demanding / (c) reservations in jobs / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'deaf' with ' the deaf' . 'The deaf' represents the whole community of deafs. === PAGE 16 ===

questions.question: (a) The book's cover / (b) is highly / (c)glossy / (d) no error.
questions.correction: Replace 'book's cover' with 'the cover of the book'.
questions.solution: Replace 'book's cover' with 'the cover of the book'. For non-living things, we use 'of' in place of apostrophe s.

questions.question: (a) The scissors / (b) which is lying on the table / (c)can't be used now / (d) no error. === PAGE 12 ===

options.b: (b) which is lying on the table

questions.solution: Replace 'is' with 'are'. The noun 'scissors' is plural and a plural verb is used with it.

questions.question: (a) Pair after pair / (b) of binoculars have been / (c)sent to Mr. Rajkumar / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'have' with 'has'. If we use a preposition after a noun and the same noun is repeated after the preposition, both the nouns should be in singular, and a singular verb will be used.

questions.question: (a) He received a / (b) summon to appear in court / (c) for the murder case / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'summon' with 'summons'. 'Summons' is a singular noun and a singular verb is used with it.

questions.question: (a) Mathematics play a critical / (b) role in various fields like / (c) science, engineering, and finance. / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'play' with 'plays'. The name of the subject ending with 's' appears as plural but they are singular nouns and a singular verb is used with them.

questions.question: (a) You will see that different people / (b) living in India / (c) have different cultures / (d) no error.

options.a: (a) You will see that different people

questions.solution: Replace 'people' with 'peoples'. 'People' is a plural noun and never takes s / es. But when it describes the meaning of race, nation or tribes, the use of 'peoples' is absolutely correct. 'Peoples' is a countable noun.

questions.question: (a) Peoples / (b)toil and moil to earn / (c)their bread and butter / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'peoples' with 'people'. 'People' is a plural noun and never takes s / es when used in the general sense.

questions.question: (a) Can you give / (b) me your half hour / (c) to finish this work? / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'half hour' with 'half an hour'. The noun 'half' is always written as 'half a / an noun' or 'a half noun'.

questions.question: (a) Three hundred rupees / (b) are not a reasonable price / (c) for this book / (d) no error.
questions.solution: replace 'are' with 'is'. The amount of money, distance and time are considered as singular units and singular verbs are used with them.

questions.question: (a) Payal is going / (b) to buy a four / (c) rooms flat tomorrow / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'rooms' with 'room'. When a compound noun(four room) is used before another noun(flat) as an adjective, it is kept in singular form.

questions.question: (a) Paramjeet / (b) respects a student / (c) in Karamveer / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'a' with 'the'. The use of 'the' with any common noun acts as the abstract noun and tells the quality of that noun.

questions.question: (a) You should / (b)take care of / (c) the olds / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'olds' with 'old'. 'The old' represents all the old people.

questions.question: (a) The police / (b) has arrived on the spot / (c)on time / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace ' has' with ' have'. Police is a plural noun and hence always takes a plural verb.

questions.question: (a) Rabies are / (b) a dangerous / (c)disease / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'are' with 'is'. The name of any disease is always a singular noun and hence takes a singular verb.

questions.question: (a) Everything's beauty / (b) is difficult / (c) to define. / (d) no error.
questions.correction: Replace 'everything's beauty' with 'The beauty of everything' The words 'everything, nothing, something, anything' never takes apostrophes with them.
questions.solution: Replace 'everything's beauty' with 'The beauty of everything' The words 'everything, nothing, something, anything' never takes apostrophes with them.

questions.question: (a) Poor are / (b) exploited by / (c) the rich / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'poor' with ' the poor'. 'The poor' represents the whole community of poors.

questions.question: (a) The brave / (b) is loved and respected all over / (c) the world / (d) no error.

options.b: (b) is loved and respected all over

questions.solution: Replace 'is' with 'are'. 'The brave' represents the whole community of brave.

questions.question: (a) Her knickers, / (b) adorned with intricate lace patterns, / (c)was carefully folded in the drawer / (d) no error.

options.c: (c) was carefully folded in the drawer

questions.solution: Replace 'was' with 'were'. 'Knickers' is a plural noun and always takes a plural verb.

questions.question: (a) The news are / (b) broadcast daily to keep the public informed / (c) about current events / (d) no error.

options.b: (b) broadcast daily to keep the public informed

questions.solution: Replace 'are' with 'is'. 'News' is a singular noun and always takes a singular verb.

questions.question: (a) Diabetes require / (b)careful management of blood sugar levels / (c)through medication and lifestyle changes / (d) no error.

options.b: (b) careful management of blood sugar levels

questions.solution: Replace 'require' with 'requires'. The name of any disease is always a singular noun and hence takes a singular verb.

questions.question: (a) The gentry in the / (b) historic town have preserved their cultural / (c)heritage with great care / (d) no error.

options.b: (b) historic town have preserved their cultural

questions.solution: No error. Gentry is a plural noun and hence always takes a plural verb.

questions.question: (a) Cities after cities / (b) has witnessed significant development / (c) over the years / (d) no error.
questions.correction: Replace 'cities after cities' with 'city after city'.
questions.solution: Replace 'cities after cities' with 'city after city'. If we use a preposition after a noun and the same noun is repeated after the preposition, both the nouns should be in singular, and a singular verb will be used.

questions.question: (a) The twenty-men committee, / (b)comprising dedicated individuals from various backgrounds, collaborated seamlessly / (c) to organize the community event / (d) no error.

options.b: (b) comprising dedicated individuals from various backgrounds, collaborated seamlessly

questions.solution: Replace 'men' with 'man'. When a compound noun is used as an adjective, it is kept in singular form.

questions.question: (a) The seven-feet-tall basketball player, / (b)known for his incredible slam dunks and defensive prowess, dominated / (c) the court during the championship game / (d) no error.

options.b: (b) known for his incredible slam dunks and defensive prowess, dominated
options.c: (c) the court during the championship game

questions.solution: Replace 'feet' with 'foot'. As feet is the plural form of foot. When a compound noun is used as an adjective, it is kept in singular form.

questions.question: (a) All the informations / (b) imparted to me can't be / (c) used for this purpose / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'informations' with 'information'. 'Information' is an uncountable noun and hence does not have a plural form.

questions.question: (a) I have not gone through / (b) this history book, so i can not / (c) tell you anything about its content / (d) no error.

options.b: (b) this history book, so i can not
options.c: (c) tell you anything about its content

questions.solution: Replace 'content' with 'contents'. 'Content' means satisfaction while 'contents' is related to subject matter.

questions.question: (a) Sweet voice / (b) is one of her / (c) beauty / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'beauty' with 'beauties'. Beauty is used as a countable as well as uncountable noun. The noun 'beauty' is uncountable when it talks about the beauty of something or person but it is a countable noun when it talks about the features of something or someone. === PAGE 17 ===

questions.question: (a) Take off / (b) your cloths / (c) and have a bath / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'cloths' with 'clothes'. 'Cloth' is a material noun and hence is uncountable. It never takes s / es. But clothes means attire or clad.

questions.question: (a) I don't / (b) like the / (c) government's policies / (d) no error.
questions.solution: No error.

questions.question: (a) Sapna is not / (b) beautiful, but / (c) her hair are straight / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'are' with 'is'. 'Hair' is an uncountable noun and hence takes a singular verb.

questions.question: (a) This pair of / (b) spectacles / (c) are highly expensive / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'are' with 'is'. 'Pair of spectacles' is a singular noun and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: (a) Have you ever / (b) seen such a beautiful / (c) shoal of fishes / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'fishes' with 'fish'. Rule : Be careful with the noun fish which is normally used as the same in singular and plural form. But when it talks about the kind or type of fish, it is written as fishes.

questions.question: (a) I always / (b) have fruits / (c) in my breakfast / (d) no error. === PAGE 13 ===
questions.solution: Replace 'fruits' with 'fruit'. Rule : The noun 'fruit' is uncountable when it gives the meaning of food. But it is countable when we talk about the kind or type of fruit.

questions.question: (a) She has to appear / (b) before the / (c) metropolis magistrate / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'metropolis' with 'metropolitan'. Rule : 'Metropolis' refers to a large and densely populated industrial and commercial city but 'metropolitan' is the correct term when referring to a person related or connected to a metropolis.

questions.question: (a) Pair after pair / (b)of shoes has been / (c) sent to him / (d) no error.
questions.solution: No error. If we use a preposition after a noun and the same noun is repeated after the preposition, both the nouns should be in singular, and a singular verb will be used.

questions.question: (a) Are you talking / (b) about India / (c) and China's leaders? / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace "India" with "India's". Rule : For common possession, use 's with the final word. But to show the different possession 's is used with all the words.

questions.question: (a) Mr. Rajkumar / (b) has five / (c) wifes / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'wifes' with 'wives'. The plural form of wife is wives.

questions.question: (a) I asked / (b) the address / (c) many passer-bys / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'passer-bys' with 'passers-by'. In case of compound nouns, (except the nouns made with man / woman) use root or head word to make it plural.

questions.question: (a) Rachna has / (b) only five / (c) childs / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'childs' with 'children'. The plural form of child is children.

questions.question: (a) I need / (b) two spoonsful / (c) of sugar / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'spoonsful' with 'spoonfuls'. Nouns ending with 'ful' are made plural by putting 's' after 'ful'.

questions.question: (a) There are only two / (b) women doctor / (c) in the hospital / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'doctor' with 'doctors'. In case of compound nouns starting with man or woman, both the nouns are made plural.

questions.question: (a) Rachna's and Nancy's / (b) father is / (c) my uncle / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace "Rachna's" with "Rachna". For common possession, use 's with the final word.

questions.question: (a) I was carrying / (b) someone's else / (c) bag / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace "someone's else" with "someone else's". If else is used after 'someone', then 's will be used after else.

questions.question: (a) Have you heard about / (b) my sister's in law husband / (c) in the news? / (d) no error.
questions.correction: Replace "sister's in law" with "sister in law's".
questions.solution: Replace "sister's in law" with "sister in law's". A singular compound noun shows possession with an apostrophe + s at the end of the word.

questions.question: (a) All the peoples / (b) in North America / (c) are egoistic / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'peoples' with 'people'. 'People' refers to all the people in a region in the general sense. 'Peoples' is used when referring to different ethnic, cultural or national groups within a region.

questions.question: (a) The leader, in the midst / (b) of a heated debate, defended / (c) his proposal with passion and eloquence / (d) no error.

options.c: (c) his proposal with passion and eloquence

questions.solution: No error. The noun 'leader' is used for both Male and Female Genders and is used as singular and generally: he / his / him are used after it.

questions.question: (a) Keep your valuable secure / (b) in the hotel safe while / (c) exploring the vibrant city / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'valuable' with 'valuables' . 'Valuable' is an adjective while 'valuables' refer to items such as money, jewelry or any important documents etc.

questions.question: (a) Amidst the bustling city, the police, / (b)equipped with state-of-the-art technology / (c) is tirelessly working to ensure the safety of the diverse population. / (d) no error.

options.a: (a) Amidst the bustling city, the police,
options.c: (c) is tirelessly working to ensure the safety of the diverse population.

questions.solution: Replace 'is' with 'are'. 'Police' is a plural noun and hence always takes a plural verb.

questions.question: (a) She bought / (b)a beautiful handmade paper / (c)to write a letter to her friend / (d) no error

options.c: (c) to write a letter to her friend

questions.solution: No error.

questions.question: (a) The artist carefully / (b) selected different types of / (c) papers for her origami creations / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'papers' with 'paper'. (Here, paper is a material noun, so it is treated as a singular noun.)

questions.question: (a) The blacksmith / (b) forged intricate designs / (c) using irons in his workshop / (d) no error.
questions.solution: Replace 'irons' with 'iron'. Here, 'iron' is a material noun while irons means a fetter or chain.

questions.question: (a) The archaeologists discovered / (b) ancient artifacts buried / (c) in the grounds during the excavation / (d) no error.

options.c: (c) in the grounds during the excavation

options.b: (b) her wit end trying to fix

options.b: (b) advanced topics will be delivered by
options.c: (c) renowned experts during the academic conference

questions.solution: Replace 'lecture' with 'lectures'. Here, the sentence talks about multiple lectures so plural form of lecture will be used.
